misc.t: ‘Bowling in good area, play with patience’: Akash Deep on how post-Lunch burst came on Day 1 of IND vs NZ 2nd Test
misc.sum: Akash Deep powered India’s post-Lunch burst on Day 1 of their second Test against New Zealand on Friday and the pacer explained that their tactics was straightforward – bowl in good areas and be patient. Three Kiwi wickets fell in three consecutive overs, two of them to Deep and one to Anshul Kamboj.
pts: Deep started the burst by dismissing the set New Zealand captain Tom Latham after which Kamboj dismissed the hosts’ first Test hero Henry Nicholls.
So we did that, and we got three wickets,” Akash told reporters after the day’s play, at which point New Zealand’s score read 246/5 in 85 overs.

While the Christchurch surface is also expected to get easier to bat on over the course of the Test, Deep feels that there might better assistance for bowlers here than what was the case in Wellington.

misc.t: New Zealand’s Tom Blundell opens up on difficulty of being one-format player
misc.sum: New Zealand batter Tom Blundell opened up on the difficulty of being a one-format player after staying unbeaten on 53 at the end of the opening day’s play of the second India vs New Zealand Test match . “I look back to last season and domestic cricket.
pts: You go through periods where you might not play Test cricket for three or four months and then all of a sudden you’re playing Test cricket in India,” he said.
The batter also said he is happy with the 246/5 that his team managed and the “big job” now is to take it past 300 on the challenging track that’s “nipping quite a lot”.
“It was a little bit slow from all counts initially, but yeah throughout the whole day, it was nipping quite a lot… (we will) take it 100 per cent.
